title: Photonz uses little memory, and what made it use 4 GB is found and fixed
goal: Photonz stays light on memory however long it has been open and whatever you do in it, and lets go of what it no longer needs. A colleague saw it use about 4 GB. Find out what caused that, fix it, and set a memory budget that a test holds the app to from now on.
notes: User, 2026-10-23: 'a colleague was saying photonz was consuming like 4 gigs. there must be a memory leak. please make a task a goal to use low memory and evaluate what might have caused the high usage.' A leak is the user's guess and is NOT confirmed. We don't know which version, release or session the colleague had. Measured on this Mac by the intake window at 2026-10-23 (footprint -p): the Photonz Dev app itself is 128 MB after 1h55m. Two helpers it started 3 minutes earlier for Ask: llama-server (dist/Photonz Dev.app/Contents/Helpers/AskModel, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M) is 4,831 MB footprint, with RSS shown as 22.6 GB because of the mapped model file. The picture model, python server.py under Application Support/Photonz/Models/picture-tools, is 4,757 MB footprint. So the strongest SUSPECT for '4 GB' is the Ask helpers, since Activity Monitor may show them under Photonz. Check that, and check how a person would see it. The others are long-session growth in the app itself, which has not been measured. The idle release for the chat server is in AskModelServer.swift:159-182 (AskBuiltInServerPlan.isIdle). Not checked whether AskPictureModel.swift has the same. Helper start and stop is AskHelperProcess.swift. Possibly relevant: should the default model be smaller on a Mac with less memory (AskModels.recommended picks by memory)? Say in the audit what a 16 GB Mac gets. Never kill or measure the person's own dev app during their session: use the probe.
acceptance: Reproduce first: a scripted long session on the probe (open and close 20 screenshots and a 12-megapixel picture, edit with layers and effects, undo and redo, scrub and play a 5-minute captioned video, open capture history, run Ask with drawing twice, leave it idle 10 minutes). Record the footprint of Photonz and of each helper it starts (footprint -p, not RSS) every minute, as a chart in the audit. That is the before

Name each cause found, with the measurement that proves it: a leak (Instruments Leaks or the leaks tool, or memory that only grows across repeated open/close), caches with no limit (ImageStore, thumbnails, capture history, video frames, render textures), undo history holding whole bitmaps, the Ask helpers. For each one, say whether a person sees it in Activity Monitor as Photonz

Fix what was found, then set and write down the budget. Photonz on its own: under about 300 MB idle with one screenshot open, and back within 20 percent of that after the long session once windows are closed. Caches have a size limit and shrink under memory pressure. The audit has the after chart

The Ask helpers (the chat model server and the picture model) start only when Ask needs them, and are let go after a few idle minutes and when Photonz quits. Each one's footprint while loaded and after release is in the audit, and the picture model obeys the same idle rule as the chat model
A test runs the open/close loop and fails if memory keeps growing across repeats (a leak guard), and a memory check after the long session joins the rotating walk check

Audit under queue/audits/ with the before and after charts; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Reproduced first on the probe: 20 screenshots and five 12 MP pictures opened and closed took Photonz from 400 MB to 1.96 GB, never coming back (Scripts/memory-watch.sh). heap on a memory graph: 25 EditorState alive after 25 windows closed. leaks --traceTree named the holders: the walk harness's strong editor list (20 of them, probe only), the inspector fold store's closure (a retain cycle with the panel's @State), ToolBarLayoutProbe.shared.pickMoreRow (every build), and a closed window AppKit keeps.

Fixed: harness holds editors weakly; InspectorPanel clears folds.onFoldFromAnotherWindow on disappear; ToolBarLayoutProbe registers only in the probe; EditorState.letGoOnClose empties store, renderers, frame, thumbnails on the window's willClose (and drops frames still in flight). Guard proven: putting the fold cycle back turns closed-windows-give-their-memory-back-walk red with '13 editors are still in memory'.

Chose MallocLargeCache=0 (Info.plist LSEnvironment, checked by build-app.sh) over keeping the allocator's large cache because on macOS 26 freed large blocks stay in the footprint at the session's peak and malloc_zone_pressure_relief does not release them (test program: 8x48 MB freed stays 367 MB; with the setting, back to 1 MB). Cost on render perf tests: full 12 MP 27.2 to 28.1 ms, interactive 5.4 ms unchanged, export about 4 percent.

Long session (Scripts/memory-session.sh), Photonz itself. Before: 203 MB one screenshot, 693 after 20 screenshots (21 editors), 1430 editing 12 MP, 1247 idle with all closed (26 editors). After: 165, 87, 501, 180 (3 emptied editors). Ask helpers: llama-server about 3 GB, picture model 13 GB painting and 5 GB loaded, both let go about 5 min after Ask's last drawing and within 2 s of quit; responsible process of both is Photonz. 16 GB Mac: Gemma 4 E4B, picture model not offered.

left rough: up to 3 closed windows' editors stay reachable after a long session via a closed window AppKit keeps (SwiftUI focus storage, menu observation); each already emptied, so no one sees it. Did not file: under the bar. Quick guard allows 1, long session 3.

left rough: section-fold-motion-walk failed twice then passed on this build with two different failures (an 18.5 ms pass, then Speed missing); already listed on walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26 from before this change, so nothing new filed.

Audit rough items are measured facts or logged above; none filed (no defect a person would see remains). closed-windows-give-their-memory-back-walk joins every rotating check (queue/bin/sweep-schedule.mjs everyCheck).

Found and fixed what made Photonz grow: closed windows stayed in memory (inspector fold-store retain cycle, a tool bar walk hook in every build, the walk harness's strong list), and macOS 26's allocator kept freed pictures counted (MallocLargeCache=0 via LSEnvironment). Editors now empty themselves on close; memory pressure clears render caches. Long session, Photonz idle with all closed: 1247 MB before, 180 MB after; one screenshot 165 MB (budget 300). Budget in docs/design/memory.md + MemoryBudget (tested); walk step memory; closed-windows-give-their-memory-back-walk in every rotating check (proven red with the cycle put back). Ask helpers measured: chat ~3 GB, picture model 13 GB painting / 5 GB loaded, both released 5 idle min after use and within 2 s of quit. Charts and audit: queue/audits/2026-10-23-photonz-uses-little-memory.json. Commit 38e4992c; Scripts/test.sh green (14,317).
